title: Quantizer-Aware Hierarchical Neural Codec Modeling for Speech Deepfake Detection
summary: Neural audio codecs discretize speech via residual vector quantization (RVQ), forming a coarse-to-fine hierarchy across quantizers. While codec models have been explored for representation learning, their discrete structure remains underutilized in speech deepfake detection. In particular, different quantization levels capture complementary acoustic cues, where early quantizers encode coarse structure and later quantizers refine residual details that reveal synthesis artifacts. Existing systems either rely on continuous encoder features or ignore this quantizer-level hierarchy. We propose a hierarchy-aware representation learning framework that models quantizer-level contributions through learnable global weighting, enabling structured codec representations aligned with forensic cues. Keeping the speech encoder backbone frozen and updating only 4.4% additional parameters, our method achieves relative EER reductions of 46.2% on ASVspoof 2019 and 13.9% on ASVspoof5 over strong baselines.

AI.tldr: A hierarchy-aware representation learning framework for speech deepfake detection that leverages the complementary acoustic cues in neural audio codec quantizers, achieving significant performance improvements with minimal parameter updates.
AI.motivation: Neural audio codecs use residual vector quantization (RVQ) to create coarse-to-fine hierarchies, but existing speech deepfake detection systems either use continuous encoder features or ignore the quantizer-level hierarchy, missing the complementary forensic cues captured at different quantization levels.
AI.method: Proposes a hierarchy-aware representation learning framework with learnable global weighting to model quantizer-level contributions, keeping the speech encoder backbone frozen while updating only 4.4% additional parameters to align codec representations with forensic cues.
AI.result: Achieves relative EER reductions of 46.2% on ASVspoof 2019 and 13.9% on ASVspoof5 over strong baselines, demonstrating significant improvement in speech deepfake detection performance with minimal parameter updates.
AI.conclusion: The quantizer-level hierarchy in neural audio codecs provides valuable complementary acoustic cues for speech deepfake detection, and structured modeling of these contributions through learnable weighting enables effective forensic representation learning with minimal computational overhead.

title: Music Source Restoration with Ensemble Separation and Targeted Reconstruction
summary: The Inaugural Music Source Restoration (MSR) Challenge targets the recovery of original, unprocessed stems from fully mixed and mastered music. Unlike conventional music source separation, MSR requires reversing complex production processes such as equalization, compression, reverberation, and other real-world degradations. To address MSR, we propose a two-stage system. First, an ensemble of pre-trained separation models produces preliminary source estimates. Then a set of pre-trained BSRNN-based restoration models performs targeted reconstruction to refine these estimates. On the official MSR benchmark, our system surpasses the baselines on all metrics, ranking second among all submissions. The code is available at https://github.com/xinghour/Music-source-restoration-CUPAudioGroup

AI.tldr: A two-stage system combining separation models and BSRNN-based restoration models achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Music Source Restoration Challenge, ranking second among submissions.
AI.motivation: The Music Source Restoration Challenge addresses the more complex problem of recovering original, unprocessed stems from fully mixed and mastered music, which requires reversing complex production processes like equalization, compression, reverberation, and other real-world degradations beyond conventional source separation.
AI.method: A two-stage system: first, an ensemble of pre-trained separation models produces preliminary source estimates; second, a set of pre-trained BSRNN-based restoration models performs targeted reconstruction to refine these estimates.
AI.result: The system surpasses all baseline methods on the official MSR benchmark metrics and ranks second among all submissions in the challenge.
AI.conclusion: The proposed two-stage approach combining separation and restoration models effectively addresses the Music Source Restoration problem, demonstrating superior performance over existing baselines and achieving competitive ranking in the challenge.

title: Modeling Overlapped Speech with Shuffles
summary: We propose to model parallel streams of data, such as overlapped speech, using shuffles. Specifically, this paper shows how the shuffle product and partial order finite-state automata (FSAs) can be used for alignment and speaker-attributed transcription of overlapped speech. We train using the total score on these FSAs as a loss function, marginalizing over all possible serializations of overlapping sequences at subword, word, and phrase levels. To reduce graph size, we impose temporal constraints by constructing partial order FSAs. We address speaker attribution by modeling (token, speaker) tuples directly. Viterbi alignment through the shuffle product FSA directly enables one-pass alignment. We evaluate performance on synthetic LibriSpeech overlaps. To our knowledge, this is the first algorithm that enables single-pass alignment of multi-talker recordings. All algorithms are implemented using k2 / Icefall.

AI.tldr: Proposes using shuffle products and partial order FSAs for single-pass alignment and speaker-attributed transcription of overlapped speech.
AI.motivation: Need to handle parallel data streams like overlapped speech with efficient single-pass alignment and speaker attribution, addressing limitations of existing multi-pass approaches.
AI.method: Uses shuffle product and partial order FSAs to model overlapping sequences; trains with total score on FSAs as loss function, marginalizing over all serializations at subword/word/phrase levels; imposes temporal constraints to reduce graph size; models (token, speaker) tuples for attribution; uses Viterbi alignment through shuffle product FSA.
AI.result: First algorithm enabling single-pass alignment of multi-talker recordings; evaluated on synthetic LibriSpeech overlaps; implemented using k2/Icefall framework.
AI.conclusion: Shuffle products and partial order FSAs provide effective framework for one-pass alignment and speaker-attributed transcription of overlapped speech.

title: Synthetic Data Domain Adaptation for ASR via LLM-based Text and Phonetic Respelling Augmentation
summary: End-to-end automatic speech recognition often degrades on domain-specific data due to scarce in-domain resources. We propose a synthetic-data-based domain adaptation framework with two contributions: (1) a large language model (LLM)-based text augmentation pipeline with a filtering strategy that balances lexical diversity, perplexity, and domain-term coverage, and (2) phonetic respelling augmentation (PRA), a novel method that introduces pronunciation variability through LLM-generated orthographic pseudo-spellings. Unlike conventional acoustic-level methods such as SpecAugment, PRA provides phonetic diversity before speech synthesis, enabling synthetic speech to better approximate real-world variability. Experimental results across four domain-specific datasets demonstrate consistent reductions in word error rate, confirming that combining domain-specific lexical coverage with realistic pronunciation variation significantly improves ASR robustness.

AI.tldr: LLM-based text augmentation with filtering and phonetic respelling improves ASR domain adaptation by generating diverse, domain-specific synthetic speech data.
AI.motivation: End-to-end ASR systems degrade on domain-specific data due to scarce in-domain resources, requiring effective domain adaptation methods.
AI.method: Two-part framework: (1) LLM-based text augmentation pipeline with filtering balancing lexical diversity, perplexity, and domain-term coverage; (2) Phonetic Respelling Augmentation (PRA) using LLM-generated orthographic pseudo-spellings to introduce pronunciation variability before speech synthesis.
AI.result: Consistent reductions in word error rate across four domain-specific datasets, demonstrating improved ASR robustness through domain-specific lexical coverage and realistic pronunciation variation.
AI.conclusion: Combining domain-specific lexical coverage with realistic pronunciation variation via LLM-based text augmentation and phonetic respelling significantly improves ASR domain adaptation performance.

title: Learnable Pulse Accumulation for On-Device Speech Recognition: How Much Attention Do You Need?
summary: Self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length, limiting transformer-based speech models on edge devices. We introduce the Learnable Pulse Accumulator (LPA), an O(n) replacement that substitutes key-query dot products with learned gating functions: content-dependent rectangular pulses, periodic windows, and position-dependent basis functions. An MSE diagnostic sweep determines per-layer replacement difficulty and ordering. Replacing 8 of 12 wav2vec2-base layers yields 10.61% word error rate (WER) on LibriSpeech test-clean, +7.24 percentage points (pp) over the 3.37% baseline, with 3.27x speedup at 120s audio on Apple M4 Pro via an optimized MLX inference path. Cross-domain validation on SepFormer speech enhancement shows all 16 intra-chunk attention layers can be replaced without collapse, suggesting the depth wall arises from linguistic computation rather than an LPA limitation. LPA's near-binary gates at inference enable dense GPU computation with no CPU-GPU synchronization, and all operations map to mobile neural accelerators.

AI.tldr: LPA replaces self-attention with O(n) learned gating functions for efficient speech models, achieving 3.27x speedup with minimal WER degradation on wav2vec2-base.
AI.motivation: Self-attention's quadratic complexity limits transformer-based speech models on edge devices, requiring more efficient alternatives that maintain performance.
AI.method: Learnable Pulse Accumulator (LPA) replaces key-query dot products with learned gating functions: content-dependent rectangular pulses, periodic windows, and position-dependent basis functions. Uses MSE diagnostic sweep to determine per-layer replacement difficulty and ordering.
AI.result: Replacing 8 of 12 wav2vec2-base layers yields 10.61% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean (+7.24pp over 3.37% baseline) with 3.27x speedup at 120s audio on Apple M4 Pro. Cross-domain validation on SepFormer shows all 16 intra-chunk attention layers can be replaced without collapse.
AI.conclusion: LPA provides efficient O(n) alternative to self-attention for speech models, with near-binary gates enabling dense GPU computation and mobile accelerator compatibility. The depth wall in speech recognition arises from linguistic computation rather than LPA limitations.

title: Beyond Deep Learning: Speech Segmentation and Phone Classification with Neural Assemblies
summary: Deep learning dominates speech processing but relies on massive datasets, global backpropagation-guided weight updates, and produces entangled representations. Assembly Calculus (AC), which models sparse neuronal assemblies via Hebbian plasticity and winner-take-all competition, offers a biologically grounded alternative, yet prior work focused on discrete symbolic inputs. We introduce an AC-based speech processing framework that operates directly on continuous speech by combining three key contributions:(i) neural encoding that converts speech into assembly-compatible spike patterns using probabilistic mel binarisation and population-coded MFCCs; (ii) a multi-area architecture organising assemblies across hierarchical timescales and classes; and (iii) cross-area update schemes for downstream tasks. Applied to two core tasks of boundary detection and segment classification, our framework detects phone (F1=0.69) and word (F1=0.61) boundaries without any weight training, and achieves 47.5% and 45.1% accuracy on phone and command recognition. These results show that AC-based dynamical systems are a viable alternative to deep learning for speech processing.

AI.tldr: Assembly Calculus-based speech processing framework achieves competitive results on boundary detection and classification tasks without weight training, offering a biologically plausible alternative to deep learning.
AI.motivation: Deep learning dominates speech processing but requires massive datasets, global backpropagation, and produces entangled representations. Assembly Calculus offers a biologically grounded alternative with sparse neuronal assemblies, but prior work only handled discrete symbolic inputs.
AI.method: Three key contributions: (1) neural encoding converting speech to assembly-compatible spike patterns using probabilistic mel binarization and population-coded MFCCs; (2) multi-area architecture organizing assemblies across hierarchical timescales and classes; (3) cross-area update schemes for downstream tasks.
AI.result: Achieves phone boundary detection (F1=0.69) and word boundary detection (F1=0.61) without weight training. Phone recognition accuracy of 47.5% and command recognition accuracy of 45.1%.
AI.conclusion: Assembly Calculus-based dynamical systems are a viable alternative to deep learning for speech processing, demonstrating competitive performance on core tasks while offering biological plausibility and avoiding weight training requirements.

title: The Voice Behind the Words: Quantifying Intersectional Bias in SpeechLLMs
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, Submitted to Interspeech 2026
summary: Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs) process spoken input directly, retaining cues such as accent and perceived gender that were previously removed in cascaded pipelines. This introduces speaker identity dependent variation in responses. We present a large-scale intersectional evaluation of accent and gender bias in three SpeechLLMs using 2,880 controlled interactions across six English accents and two gender presentations, keeping linguistic content constant through voice cloning. Using pointwise LLM-judge ratings, pairwise comparisons, and Best-Worst Scaling with human validation, we detect consistent disparities. Eastern European-accented speech receives lower helpfulness scores, particularly for female-presenting voices. The bias is implicit: responses remain polite but differ in helpfulness. While LLM judges capture the directional trend of these biases, human evaluators exhibit significantly higher sensitivity, uncovering sharper intersectional disparities.

AI.tldr: SpeechLLMs exhibit implicit intersectional bias: Eastern European-accented speech receives lower helpfulness scores, especially for female-presenting voices, despite polite responses.
AI.motivation: SpeechLLMs retain speaker identity cues (accent, perceived gender) that were previously removed in cascaded pipelines, introducing speaker-dependent variation in responses that requires systematic evaluation for bias.
AI.method: Large-scale intersectional evaluation of three SpeechLLMs using 2,880 controlled interactions across six English accents and two gender presentations, with linguistic content kept constant through voice cloning. Evaluation uses pointwise LLM-judge ratings, pairwise comparisons, and Best-Worst Scaling with human validation.
AI.result: Consistent disparities detected: Eastern European-accented speech receives lower helpfulness scores, particularly for female-presenting voices. Bias is implicit (responses remain polite but differ in helpfulness). LLM judges capture directional trend but human evaluators show significantly higher sensitivity and uncover sharper intersectional disparities.
AI.conclusion: SpeechLLMs exhibit implicit intersectional bias based on accent and gender presentation, with human evaluators being more sensitive to these disparities than LLM judges, highlighting the need for bias mitigation in speech-based language models.

title: SimulU: Training-free Policy for Long-form Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation
summary: Simultaneous speech-to-speech translation (SimulS2S) is essential for real-time multilingual communication, with increasing integration into meeting and streaming platforms. Despite this, SimulS2S remains underexplored in research, where current solutions often rely on resource-intensive training procedures and operate on short-form, pre-segmented utterances, failing to generalize to continuous speech. To bridge this gap, we propose SimulU, the first training-free policy for long-form SimulS2S. SimulU adopts history management and speech output selection strategies that exploit cross-attention in pre-trained end-to-end models to regulate both input history and output generation. Evaluations on MuST-C across 8 languages show that SimulU achieves a better or comparable quality-latency trade-off against strong cascaded models. By eliminating the need for ad-hoc training, SimulU offers a promising path to end-to-end SimulS2S in realistic, long-form scenarios.

AI.tldr: SimulU is a training-free policy for long-form simultaneous speech-to-speech translation that uses history management and speech output selection strategies based on cross-attention in pre-trained models, achieving competitive quality-latency trade-offs without additional training.
AI.motivation: Current simultaneous speech-to-speech translation solutions are resource-intensive, operate on short-form pre-segmented utterances, and fail to generalize to continuous speech, creating a gap for practical long-form applications.
AI.method: SimulU employs history management and speech output selection strategies that exploit cross-attention mechanisms in pre-trained end-to-end models to regulate both input history and output generation, requiring no additional training.
AI.result: Evaluations on MuST-C across 8 languages show SimulU achieves better or comparable quality-latency trade-off against strong cascaded models, demonstrating effectiveness without training.
AI.conclusion: SimulU offers a promising path to end-to-end simultaneous speech-to-speech translation in realistic long-form scenarios by eliminating the need for ad-hoc training.

title: Over-the-air White-box Attack on the Wav2Vec Speech Recognition Neural Network
summary: Automatic speech recognition systems based on neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that alter transcriptions in a malicious way. Recent works in this field have focused on making attacks work in over-the-air scenarios, however such attacks are typically detectable by human hearing, limiting their potential applications. In the present work we explore different approaches of making over-the-air attacks less detectable, as well as the impact these approaches have on the attacks' effectiveness.

AI.tldr: Explores methods to make over-the-air adversarial attacks on speech recognition systems less detectable to humans while maintaining effectiveness.
AI.motivation: Current over-the-air adversarial attacks on neural network-based speech recognition systems are typically detectable by human hearing, which limits their practical applications.
AI.method: Explores different approaches to reduce detectability of over-the-air adversarial attacks while examining their impact on attack effectiveness.
AI.result: The paper investigates the trade-off between attack stealthiness (reduced human detectability) and effectiveness in altering speech recognition transcriptions.
AI.conclusion: There exists a tension between making over-the-air adversarial attacks less detectable to humans and maintaining their effectiveness in manipulating speech recognition systems.

title: PowerModelsGAT-AI: Physics-Informed Graph Attention for Multi-System Power Flow with Continual Learning
summary: Solving the alternating current power flow equations in real time is essential for secure grid operation, yet classical Newton-Raphson solvers can be slow under stressed conditions. Existing graph neural networks for power flow are typically trained on a single system and often degrade on different systems. We present PowerModelsGAT-AI, a physics-informed graph attention network that predicts bus voltages and generator injections. The model uses bus-type-aware masking to handle different bus types and balances multiple loss terms, including a power-mismatch penalty, using learned weights. We evaluate the model on 14 benchmark systems (4 to 6,470 buses) and train a unified model on 13 of these under N-2 (two-branch outage) conditions, achieving an average normalized mean absolute error of 0.89% for voltage magnitudes and R^2 > 0.99 for voltage angles. We also show continual learning: when adapting a base model to a new 1,354-bus system, standard fine-tuning causes severe forgetting with error increases exceeding 1000% on base systems, while our experience replay and elastic weight consolidation strategy keeps error increases below 2% and in some cases improves base-system performance. Interpretability analysis shows that learned attention weights correlate with physical branch parameters (susceptance: r = 0.38; thermal limits: r = 0.22), and feature importance analysis supports that the model captures established power flow relationships.

AI.tldr: PowerModelsGAT-AI: A physics-informed graph attention network for AC power flow prediction with bus-type-aware masking, multi-loss balancing, and continual learning capabilities that maintains performance across different power systems.
AI.motivation: Classical Newton-Raphson solvers for AC power flow equations can be slow under stressed conditions, and existing graph neural networks typically degrade when applied to different power systems than they were trained on.
AI.method: Physics-informed graph attention network with bus-type-aware masking to handle different bus types, balancing multiple loss terms (including power-mismatch penalty) using learned weights, and incorporating continual learning strategies (experience replay and elastic weight consolidation) for adaptation to new systems.
AI.result: Achieved average normalized mean absolute error of 0.89% for voltage magnitudes and R² > 0.99 for voltage angles across 14 benchmark systems (4 to 6,470 buses). Continual learning strategy kept error increases below 2% when adapting to new systems, compared to 1000%+ increases with standard fine-tuning. Learned attention weights correlate with physical branch parameters (susceptance: r = 0.38; thermal limits: r = 0.22).
AI.conclusion: PowerModelsGAT-AI provides accurate, generalizable AC power flow prediction across diverse power systems with effective continual learning capabilities, and interpretability analysis confirms the model captures established physical relationships in power flow.

title: The Port-Hamiltonian Structure of Vehicle Manipulator Systems
summary: This paper presents a port-Hamiltonian formulation of vehicle-manipulator systems (VMS), a broad class of robotic systems including aerial manipulators, underwater manipulators, space robots, and omnidirectional mobile manipulators. Unlike existing Lagrangian formulations that obscure the underlying energetic structure, the proposed port-Hamiltonian formulation explicitly reveals the energy flow and conservation properties of these complex mechanical systems. We derive the port-Hamiltonian dynamics from first principles using Hamiltonian reduction theory. Two complementary formulations are presented: a standard form that directly exposes the energy structure, and an inertially-decoupled form that leverages the principal bundle structure of the VMS configuration space and is particularly suitable for control design and numerical simulation. The coordinate-free geometric approach we follow avoids singularities associated with local parameterizations of the base orientation. We rigorously establish the mathematical equivalence between our port-Hamiltonian formulations and existing reduced Euler-Lagrange and Boltzmann-Hamel equations found in the robotics and geometric mechanics literature.

AI.tldr: Port-Hamiltonian formulation of vehicle-manipulator systems that explicitly reveals energy flow and conservation properties, with two complementary forms for analysis and control.
AI.motivation: Existing Lagrangian formulations obscure the underlying energetic structure of vehicle-manipulator systems (VMS), which include aerial manipulators, underwater manipulators, space robots, and omnidirectional mobile manipulators. The paper aims to develop a formulation that explicitly reveals energy flow and conservation properties.
AI.method: Derived port-Hamiltonian dynamics from first principles using Hamiltonian reduction theory. Presented two complementary formulations: 1) standard form that directly exposes energy structure, and 2) inertially-decoupled form that leverages the principal bundle structure of VMS configuration space. Used coordinate-free geometric approach to avoid singularities associated with local parameterizations of base orientation.
AI.result: Developed a port-Hamiltonian formulation that explicitly reveals energy flow and conservation properties of VMS. Established mathematical equivalence between the port-Hamiltonian formulations and existing reduced Euler-Lagrange and Boltzmann-Hamel equations from robotics and geometric mechanics literature.
AI.conclusion: The port-Hamiltonian formulation provides a superior framework for analyzing and controlling vehicle-manipulator systems by explicitly revealing their energetic structure, with the inertially-decoupled form being particularly suitable for control design and numerical simulation.

title: Shared Representation Learning for Reference-Guided Targeted Sound Detection
summary: Human listeners exhibit the remarkable ability to segregate a desired sound from complex acoustic scenes through selective auditory attention, motivating the study of Targeted Sound Detection (TSD). The task requires detecting and localizing a target sound in a mixture when a reference audio of that sound is provided. Prior approaches, rely on generating a sound-discriminative conditional embedding vector for the reference and pairing it with a mixture encoder, jointly optimized with a multi-task learning approach. In this work, we propose a unified encoder architecture that processes both the reference and mixture audio within a shared representation space, promoting stronger alignment while reducing architectural complexity. This design choice not only simplifies the overall framework but also enhances generalization to unseen classes. Following the multi-task training paradigm, our method achieves substantial improvements over prior approaches, surpassing existing methods and establishing a new state-of-the-art benchmark for targeted sound detection, with a segment-level F1 score of 83.15% and an overall accuracy of 95.17% on the URBAN-SED dataset.

AI.tldr: Proposes unified encoder architecture for Targeted Sound Detection that processes reference and mixture audio in shared representation space, achieving state-of-the-art performance with 83.15% F1 score and 95.17% accuracy on URBAN-SED dataset.
AI.motivation: Human auditory attention enables sound segregation in complex scenes, motivating Targeted Sound Detection (TSD). Prior approaches use separate embeddings and encoders, lacking strong alignment between reference and mixture representations.
AI.method: Unified encoder architecture processes both reference and mixture audio within a shared representation space, promoting stronger alignment while reducing architectural complexity. Uses multi-task training paradigm for joint optimization.
AI.result: Achieves substantial improvements over prior approaches, establishing new state-of-the-art: 83.15% segment-level F1 score and 95.17% overall accuracy on URBAN-SED dataset. Shows enhanced generalization to unseen classes.
AI.conclusion: Shared representation space between reference and mixture audio simplifies architecture while improving performance and generalization, demonstrating effectiveness of unified encoder approach for Targeted Sound Detection.

title: Cleaner energy microgrids under market power and limited regulation in developing countries
summary: In many low-income countries, neighborhood diesel generators are widely used to compensate for unreliable or unavailable national electricity grids. These diesel-based microgrids are typically characterized by market power, significant pollution, and weak regulatory oversight. In parallel, households increasingly deploy off-grid solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to gain control over electricity supply. However, these systems suffer from curtailed excess generation during peak solar hours and unreliable access at other times. While prior studies have optimized microgrids in developing contexts from a techno-economic perspective, they largely neglect the market power exerted by monopolistic private generators. This paper addresses this gap by developing a bi-level game-theoretic model that enables household-generated electricity to be fed into the microgrid while explicitly accounting for the market power of a neighborhood diesel generator company (DGC). The regulator sets price and feed-in-tariff caps to maximize household economic surplus (HES), while the DGC acts as a profit-maximizing agent controlling access and supply. The model is applied to a Lebanese case study using high-resolution empirical data collected via logging devices. Results show that: (i) price and feed-in-tariff caps substantially increase HES and consistently induce significant household PV feed-in to the microgrid; (ii) higher DGC budgets or greater PV-owner penetration lead to pronounced gains in HES; and (iii) the renewable energy share reaches 60% under base conditions and approaches 100% at sufficiently high budgets or PV-owner penetration levels, compared to 0% under the status quo.

AI.tldr: A game-theoretic model addresses market power in diesel microgrids by enabling household PV feed-in with regulatory price caps, showing significant renewable energy adoption and household economic benefits in Lebanese case study.
AI.motivation: Diesel microgrids in low-income countries suffer from market power, pollution, and weak regulation, while household PV systems face curtailment and reliability issues. Existing studies neglect monopolistic market power in microgrid optimization.
AI.method: Developed a bi-level game-theoretic model where regulator sets price and feed-in-tariff caps to maximize household economic surplus, while diesel generator company acts as profit-maximizing agent controlling access and supply. Applied to Lebanese case study using high-resolution empirical data from logging devices.
AI.result: Price and feed-in-tariff caps substantially increase household economic surplus and induce significant PV feed-in; higher DGC budgets or greater PV-owner penetration lead to pronounced HES gains; renewable energy share reaches 60% under base conditions and approaches 100% at high budgets/PV penetration, compared to 0% status quo.
AI.conclusion: Regulatory intervention through price caps and feed-in tariffs can effectively counter market power in diesel microgrids, enabling significant renewable energy integration and substantial household economic benefits in developing country contexts.

title: Uncertainty Quantification and Risk Control for Multi-Speaker Sound Source Localization
summary: Reliable Sound Source Localization (SSL) plays an essential role in many downstream tasks, where informed decision making depends not only on accurate localization but also on the confidence in each estimate. This need for reliability becomes even more pronounced in challenging conditions, such as reverberant environments and multi-source scenarios. However, existing SSL methods typically provide only point estimates, offering limited or no Uncertainty Quantification (UQ). We leverage the Conformal Prediction (CP) framework and its extensions for controlling general risk functions to develop two complementary UQ approaches for SSL. The first assumes that the number of active sources is known and constructs prediction regions that cover the true source locations. The second addresses the more challenging setting where the source count is unknown, first reliably estimating the number of active sources and then forming corresponding prediction regions. We evaluate the proposed methods on extensive simulations and real-world recordings across varying reverberation levels and source configurations. Results demonstrate reliable finite-sample guarantees and consistent performance for both known and unknown source-count scenarios, highlighting the practical utility of the proposed frameworks for uncertainty-aware SSL.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes two conformal prediction-based uncertainty quantification methods for sound source localization that provide reliable confidence estimates in challenging acoustic environments.
AI.motivation: Existing SSL methods only provide point estimates without uncertainty quantification, which is insufficient for reliable decision-making in downstream tasks, especially in challenging conditions like reverberation and multi-source scenarios.
AI.method: Two complementary UQ approaches using Conformal Prediction framework: 1) Known source count - constructs prediction regions covering true source locations; 2) Unknown source count - first reliably estimates number of active sources, then forms corresponding prediction regions.
AI.result: Methods demonstrate reliable finite-sample guarantees and consistent performance across varying reverberation levels and source configurations in both simulations and real-world recordings.
AI.conclusion: The proposed conformal prediction frameworks provide practical uncertainty-aware SSL with reliable guarantees for both known and unknown source-count scenarios.

title: Stability Guarantees for Data-Driven Predictive Control of Nonlinear Systems via Approximate Koopman Embeddings
summary: Data-driven model predictive control based on Willems' fundamental lemma has proven effective for linear systems, but extending stability guarantees to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. In this paper, we establish conditions under which data-driven MPC, applied directly to input-output data from a nonlinear system, yields practical exponential stability. The key insight is that the existence of an approximate Koopman linear embedding certifies that the nonlinear data can be interpreted as noisy data from a linear time-invariant system, enabling the application of existing robust stability theories. Crucially, the Koopman embedding serves only as a theoretical certificate; the controller itself operates on raw nonlinear data without knowledge of the lifting functions. We further show that the proportional structure of the embedding residual can be exploited to obtain an ultimate bound that depends only on the irreducible offset, rather than the worst-case embedding error. The framework is demonstrated on a synchronous generator connected to an infinite bus, for which we construct an explicit physics-informed embedding with error bounds.

AI.tldr: Data-driven MPC for nonlinear systems achieves practical exponential stability by leveraging approximate Koopman embeddings as theoretical certificates, enabling application of robust linear stability theory to raw nonlinear data.
AI.motivation: While data-driven MPC based on Willems' fundamental lemma works well for linear systems, extending stability guarantees to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. The paper aims to establish conditions for practical exponential stability when applying data-driven MPC directly to input-output data from nonlinear systems.
AI.method: The approach uses approximate Koopman linear embeddings as theoretical certificates that nonlinear data can be interpreted as noisy data from a linear time-invariant system. This enables application of existing robust stability theories. The controller operates directly on raw nonlinear data without knowledge of lifting functions. The proportional structure of embedding residuals is exploited to obtain ultimate bounds dependent only on irreducible offset rather than worst-case error.
AI.result: The paper establishes conditions under which data-driven MPC applied to nonlinear system data yields practical exponential stability. The framework is demonstrated on a synchronous generator connected to an infinite bus, where an explicit physics-informed embedding with error bounds is constructed.
AI.conclusion: Approximate Koopman embeddings provide a theoretical foundation for extending data-driven MPC stability guarantees to nonlinear systems, enabling controllers to operate on raw nonlinear data while maintaining stability through robust linear theory. The method leverages embedding structure to achieve improved error bounds.

title: Robust Nasality Representation Learning for Cleft Palate-Related Velopharyngeal Dysfunction Screening in Real-World Settings
comment: 2 figures. Machine learning for speech-based VPD screening under domain shift
summary: Velopharyngeal dysfunction (VPD) is characterized by inadequate velopharyngeal closure during speech and often causes hypernasality and reduced intelligibility. Although speech-based machine learning models can perform well under standardized clinical recording conditions, their performance often drops in real-world settings because of domain shift caused by differences in devices, channels, noise, and room acoustics. To improve robustness, we propose a two-stage framework for VPD screening. First, a nasality-focused speech representation is learned by supervised contrastive pre-training on an auxiliary corpus with phoneme alignments, using oral-context versus nasal-context supervision. Second, the encoder is frozen and used with lightweight classifiers on 0.5-second speech chunks, whose probabilities are aggregated to produce recording-level decisions with a fixed threshold. On an in-domain clinical cohort of 82 subjects, the proposed method achieved perfect recording-level screening performance (macro-F1 = 1.000, accuracy = 1.000). On a separate out-of-domain set of 131 heterogeneous public Internet recordings, large pretrained speech representations degraded substantially, while MFCC was the strongest baseline (macro-F1 = 0.612, accuracy = 0.641). The proposed method achieved the best out-of-domain performance (macro-F1 = 0.679, accuracy = 0.695), improving on the strongest baseline under the same evaluation protocol. These results suggest that learning a nasality-focused representation before clinical classification can reduce sensitivity to recording artifacts and improve robustness for deployable speech-based VPD screening.

AI.tldr: Two-stage framework for VPD screening: nasality-focused speech representation via supervised contrastive pre-training, then frozen encoder with lightweight classifiers on speech chunks, achieving strong in-domain performance and improved out-of-domain robustness.
AI.motivation: Speech-based machine learning models for VPD screening perform well in clinical settings but degrade in real-world conditions due to domain shift from device, channel, noise, and acoustic variations. Need for more robust models that maintain performance across heterogeneous recording environments.
AI.method: Two-stage framework: 1) Supervised contrastive pre-training on auxiliary corpus with phoneme alignments to learn nasality-focused speech representation using oral-context vs nasal-context supervision. 2) Freeze encoder and use lightweight classifiers on 0.5-second speech chunks, aggregating probabilities with fixed threshold for recording-level decisions.
AI.result: In-domain clinical cohort (82 subjects): perfect performance (macro-F1 = 1.000, accuracy = 1.000). Out-of-domain heterogeneous Internet recordings (131 subjects): MFCC baseline performed best (macro-F1 = 0.612, accuracy = 0.641), while large pretrained speech representations degraded substantially. Proposed method achieved best out-of-domain performance (macro-F1 = 0.679, accuracy = 0.695), improving over strongest baseline.
AI.conclusion: Learning nasality-focused speech representations before clinical classification reduces sensitivity to recording artifacts and improves robustness for deployable speech-based VPD screening, addressing domain shift challenges in real-world applications.

title: Enforcing Mixed State-Input Constraints with Multiple Backup Control Barrier Functions: A Projection-based Approach
summary: Ensuring the safety of control systems often requires the satisfaction of constraints on states (such as position or velocity), control inputs (such as force), and a mixture of states and inputs (such as power that depends on both velocity and force). This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for enforcing mixed state-input constraints through a generalization of backup control barrier functions (backup CBFs). First, we extend the backup CBF approach to maintain multiple decoupled state and input constraints using a single backup set-backup controller pair. Second, we address mixed state-input constraints by converting them into state constraints using a projection from the state-input space to the state space along the backup controller. In the special case of decoupled state and input constraints, the proposed method simplifies the synthesis of backup CBFs by eliminating the need for saturating backup control laws. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method on an inverted pendulum example, where constraints on the angle (state), torque (input), and power (mixture of state and input) are satisfied simultaneously.

AI.tldr: A safety-critical control framework using generalized backup control barrier functions to enforce mixed state-input constraints, with applications to inverted pendulum systems.
AI.motivation: Control systems require safety guarantees for various constraint types including states, inputs, and mixed state-input combinations (like power). Existing methods need improvement for handling mixed constraints efficiently.
AI.method: Generalizes backup CBFs to handle multiple decoupled constraints with single backup set-controller pair, converts mixed constraints to state constraints via projection along backup controller, and simplifies synthesis by eliminating need for saturating backup control laws.
AI.result: Demonstrated efficacy on inverted pendulum system, successfully satisfying angle (state), torque (input), and power (mixed state-input) constraints simultaneously.
AI.conclusion: Proposed framework provides systematic approach for enforcing mixed state-input constraints using generalized backup CBFs, with simplified synthesis and practical applicability to complex control systems.

title: Multi-Source Evidence Fusion for Audio Question Answering
summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) can answer questions about speech, music, and environmental sounds, yet their internal reasoning is largely opaque and difficult to validate. We describe TalTech's solution to the Agent Track of the Interspeech 2026 Audio Reasoning Challenge, in which systems are evaluated on reasoning process quality, specifically the factual accuracy, logical soundness, and completeness of their reasoning chains. Our multi-source ensemble pipeline uses two LALMs that generate independent observations, while a separate text-only reasoning model cross-checks these against outputs from 25 acoustic tools organized into reliability tiers. By grounding every inference step in explicit, reliability-tagged evidence, the system produces dense, verifiable reasoning chains. Our system ranked first in the challenge, outperforming all competing systems by a wide margin in challenge's reasoning quality metric.

AI.tldr: TalTech's winning solution for Interspeech 2026 Audio Reasoning Challenge uses multi-source ensemble pipeline with LALMs and acoustic tools to produce verifiable reasoning chains.
AI.motivation: Large audio language models (LALMs) can answer questions about audio content but their internal reasoning is opaque and difficult to validate, creating a need for systems with transparent, verifiable reasoning processes.
AI.method: Multi-source ensemble pipeline using two LALMs that generate independent observations, combined with a separate text-only reasoning model that cross-checks these against outputs from 25 acoustic tools organized into reliability tiers, grounding every inference step in explicit, reliability-tagged evidence.
AI.result: The system ranked first in the Interspeech 2026 Audio Reasoning Challenge, outperforming all competing systems by a wide margin in the challenge's reasoning quality metric.
AI.conclusion: By combining multiple LALMs with a comprehensive set of acoustic tools and explicit evidence grounding, the system achieves superior reasoning quality with transparent, verifiable reasoning chains that address the opacity problem of standalone LALMs.

title: Neural-NPV Control: Learning Parameter-Dependent Controllers and Lyapunov Functions with Neural Networks
summary: Nonlinear parameter-varying (NPV) systems are a class of nonlinear systems whose dynamics explicitly depend on time-varying external parameters, making them suitable for modeling real-world systems with dynamics variations. Traditional synthesis methods for NPV systems, such as sum-of-squares (SOS) optimization, are only applicable to control-affine systems, face scalability challenges and often lead to conservative results due to structural restrictions. To address these limitations, we propose Neural-NPV, a two-stage learning-based framework that leverages neural networks to jointly synthesize a PD controller and a PD Lyapunov function for an NPV system under input constraints. In the first stage, we utilize a computationally cheap, gradient-based counterexample-guided procedure to synthesize an approximately valid PD Lyapunov function and a PD controller. In the second stage, a level-set guided refinement is then conducted to obtain a valid Lyapunov function and controller while maximizing the robust region of attraction (R-ROA). We demonstrate the advantages of Neural-NPV in terms of applicability, performance, and scalability compared to SOS-based methods through numerical experiments involving an simple inverted pendulum with one scheduling parameter and a quadrotor system with three scheduling parameters.

AI.tldr: Neural-NPV: A two-stage learning framework using neural networks to synthesize PD controllers and Lyapunov functions for nonlinear parameter-varying systems, overcoming limitations of traditional SOS methods.
AI.motivation: Traditional synthesis methods for nonlinear parameter-varying (NPV) systems (like sum-of-squares optimization) have limitations: they only work for control-affine systems, face scalability issues, and produce conservative results due to structural restrictions.
AI.method: Two-stage learning framework: 1) Gradient-based counterexample-guided synthesis of approximately valid PD Lyapunov function and PD controller; 2) Level-set guided refinement to obtain valid Lyapunov function and controller while maximizing robust region of attraction.
AI.result: Demonstrated advantages over SOS-based methods in applicability, performance, and scalability through numerical experiments on an inverted pendulum (1 scheduling parameter) and quadrotor system (3 scheduling parameters).
AI.conclusion: Neural-NPV provides a more flexible, scalable, and less conservative approach to NPV system control synthesis compared to traditional SOS methods, enabling broader applicability to complex real-world systems.

title: The Silent Thought: Modeling Internal Cognition in Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models via Latent Reasoning
summary: During conversational interactions, humans subconsciously engage in concurrent thinking while listening to a speaker. Although this internal cognitive processing may not always manifest as explicit linguistic structures, it is instrumental in formulating high-quality responses. Inspired by this cognitive phenomenon, we propose a novel Full-duplex LAtent and Internal Reasoning method named FLAIR that conducts latent thinking simultaneously with speech perception. Unlike conventional "thinking" mechanisms in NLP, which require post-hoc generation, our approach aligns seamlessly with spoken dialogue systems: during the user's speaking phase, it recursively feeds the latent embedding output from the previous step into the next step, enabling continuous reasoning that strictly adheres to causality without introducing additional latency. To enable this latent reasoning, we design an Evidence Lower Bound-based objective that supports efficient supervised finetuning via teacher forcing, circumventing the need for explicit reasoning annotations. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this think-while-listening design, which achieves competitive results on a range of speech benchmarks. Furthermore, FLAIR robustly handles conversational dynamics and attains competitive performance on full-duplex interaction metrics.

AI.tldr: FLAIR is a full-duplex latent reasoning method that enables AI to think while listening in spoken dialogue, mimicking human concurrent cognitive processing without adding latency.
AI.motivation: Inspired by human subconscious concurrent thinking during listening, the authors aim to develop AI systems that can perform latent reasoning simultaneously with speech perception, unlike conventional NLP approaches that require post-hoc generation.
AI.method: FLAIR recursively feeds latent embeddings from previous steps into subsequent steps during user speech, enabling continuous causal reasoning. It uses an Evidence Lower Bound-based objective for supervised finetuning via teacher forcing, eliminating need for explicit reasoning annotations.
AI.result: The method achieves competitive results on speech benchmarks and robustly handles conversational dynamics with competitive performance on full-duplex interaction metrics.
AI.conclusion: FLAIR successfully implements think-while-listening capability for spoken dialogue systems, demonstrating that latent concurrent reasoning can be effectively integrated without introducing additional latency.

title: Convexity and Optimal Online Control of Grid-Interfacing Converters with Current Limits
summary:
Converter-based generators and loads are growing in prevalence on power grids across the globe. The rise of these resources necessitates controllers that handle the power electronic devices' strict current limits without jeopardizing stability or overly constraining behavior. Existing controllers often employ complex, cascaded control loop architecture to saturate currents, but these controllers are challenging to tune properly and can destabilize following large disturbances.
  In this paper, we extend previous analysis to prove the feasible output region of a grid-connected converter is convex regardless of filter topology. We then formulate a convex optimal control problem from which we derive a projected gradient descent-based controller with convergence guarantees. This approach drives the converter toward optimality in real-time and differs from conventional control strategies that regulate converter outputs around predefined references regardless of surrounding grid conditions. Simulation results demonstrate safe and stabilizing behavior of the proposed controller, in both the single-converter-infinite-bus systems and multi-converter networks.

AI.tldr: A convex optimal control approach for grid-connected converters with guaranteed convergence and safe operation under current limits.
AI.motivation: The increasing prevalence of converter-based generators and loads requires controllers that handle strict current limits without compromising stability or overly constraining behavior. Existing controllers with complex cascaded control loops are difficult to tune and can destabilize after large disturbances.
AI.method: Extends previous analysis to prove the feasible output region of grid-connected converters is convex regardless of filter topology. Formulates a convex optimal control problem and derives a projected gradient descent-based controller with convergence guarantees that drives converters toward optimality in real-time.
AI.result: Simulation results demonstrate safe and stabilizing behavior of the proposed controller in both single-converter-infinite-bus systems and multi-converter networks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed convex optimal control approach provides a stable, safe alternative to conventional control strategies that regulate converter outputs around predefined references without considering surrounding grid conditions.

title: Integral Quadratic Constraints for Repeated ReLU
summary: This paper presents a new dynamic integral quadratic constraint (IQC) for the repeated Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU). These dynamic IQCs can be used to analyze stability and induced $\ell_2$-gain performance of discrete-time, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with ReLU activation functions. These analysis conditions can be incorporated into learning-based controller synthesis methods, which currently rely on static IQCs. We show that our proposed dynamic IQCs for repeated ReLU form a superset of the dynamic IQCs for repeated, slope-restricted nonlinearities. We also prove that the $\ell_2$-gain bounds are nonincreasing with respect to the horizon used in the dynamic IQC filter. A numerical example using a simple (academic) RNN shows that our proposed IQCs lead to less conservative bounds than existing IQCs.

AI.tldr: Proposes new dynamic IQCs for repeated ReLU activations in RNNs, enabling less conservative stability and performance analysis compared to existing static IQCs.
AI.motivation: Current learning-based controller synthesis methods rely on static IQCs for ReLU activations, which can be conservative. There's a need for more accurate analysis tools for stability and performance of RNNs with ReLU activations.
AI.method: Develops new dynamic integral quadratic constraints (IQCs) specifically for repeated ReLU activation functions in discrete-time RNNs. These dynamic IQCs form a superset of existing dynamic IQCs for repeated slope-restricted nonlinearities.
AI.result: The proposed dynamic IQCs provide less conservative ℓ₂-gain bounds than existing IQCs, as demonstrated in a numerical example with an academic RNN. The ℓ₂-gain bounds are proven to be nonincreasing with respect to the horizon used in the dynamic IQC filter.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic IQCs for repeated ReLU offer improved analysis tools for RNN stability and performance, enabling less conservative bounds that can enhance learning-based controller synthesis methods.

title: Linear-Quadratic Gaussian Games with Distributed Sparse Estimation
summary: Linear-quadratic Gaussian games provide a framework for modeling strategic interactions in multi-agent systems, where agents must estimate system states from noisy observations while also making decisions to optimize a quadratic cost. However, these formulations usually require agents to utilize the full set of available observations when forming their state estimates, which can be unrealistic in large-scale or resource-constrained settings. In this paper, we consider linear-quadratic Gaussian games with sparse interagent observations. To enforce sparsity in the estimation stage, we design a distributed estimator that balances estimation effectiveness with interagent measurement sparsity via a group lasso problem, while agents implement feedback Nash strategies based on their state estimates. We provide sufficient conditions under which the sparse estimator is guaranteed to trigger a corrective reset to the optimal estimation gain, ensuring that estimation quality does not degrade beyond a level determined by the regularization parameters. Simulations on a formation game show that the proposed approach yields a significant reduction in communication resources consumed while only minimally affecting the nominal equilibrium trajectories.

AI.tldr: Proposes a distributed estimator for linear-quadratic Gaussian games with sparse interagent observations, using group lasso to balance estimation quality with communication sparsity while maintaining near-optimal equilibrium performance.
AI.motivation: Standard linear-quadratic Gaussian games require agents to use all available observations for state estimation, which is unrealistic in large-scale or resource-constrained systems where communication bandwidth is limited.
AI.method: Designs a distributed estimator that enforces sparsity in interagent observations via group lasso regularization, while agents implement feedback Nash strategies based on their sparse state estimates. Provides conditions for corrective resets to optimal estimation gains.
AI.result: Theoretical analysis provides sufficient conditions for the sparse estimator to trigger corrective resets, ensuring estimation quality doesn't degrade beyond regularization parameter levels. Simulations show significant communication reduction with minimal impact on equilibrium trajectories.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach enables sparse interagent observations in linear-quadratic Gaussian games, achieving substantial communication savings while maintaining near-nominal equilibrium performance through controlled estimation quality degradation.

title: The Geometry of Coordinated Trajectories for Non-stop Flying Carriers Holding a Cable-Suspended Load
summary: This work considers the problem of using multiple aerial carriers to hold a cable-suspended load while remaining in periodic motion at all times. Using a novel differential geometric perspective, it is shown that the problem may be recast as that of finding an immersion of the unit circle into the smooth manifold of admissible configurations. Additionally, this manifold is shown to be path connected under a mild assumption on the attachment points of the carriers to the load. Based on these ideas, a family of simple linear solutions to the original problems is presented that overcomes the constraints of alternative solutions previously proposed in the literature. Simulation results demonstrate the flexibility of the theory in identifying suitable solutions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a differential geometric approach for multiple aerial carriers to hold a cable-suspended load while maintaining continuous periodic motion, showing the problem can be recast as finding an immersion of the unit circle into a path-connected configuration manifold.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to solve the problem of using multiple aerial carriers (like drones) to transport cable-suspended loads while ensuring they remain in periodic motion at all times, overcoming constraints of previous solutions in the literature.
AI.method: The method uses a novel differential geometric perspective, recasting the problem as finding an immersion of the unit circle into the smooth manifold of admissible configurations. The manifold is shown to be path-connected under mild assumptions about carrier attachment points. Based on this geometric framework, a family of simple linear solutions is developed.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that the configuration manifold is path-connected under reasonable assumptions, and presents a family of linear solutions that overcome constraints of alternative solutions. Simulation results show the flexibility of the theory in identifying suitable solutions for the aerial carrier-load system.
AI.conclusion: The differential geometric approach provides a powerful framework for solving the multi-carrier cable-suspended load problem with continuous periodic motion, offering simple linear solutions that are more flexible than previous approaches, as validated through simulations.

title: STLts-Div: Diversified Trace Synthesis from STL Specifications Using MILP (Extended Version)
summary: Modern cyber-physical systems are complex, and requirements are often written in Signal Temporal Logic (STL). Writing the right STL is difficult in practice; engineers benefit from concrete executions that illustrate what a specification actually admits. Trace synthesis addresses this need, but a single witness rarely suffices to understand intent or explore edge cases - diverse satisfying behaviors are far more informative. We introduce diversified trace synthesis: the automatic generation of sets of behaviorally diverse traces that satisfy a given STL formula. Building on a MILP encoding of STL and system model, we formalize three complementary diversification objectives - Boolean distance, random Boolean distance, and value distance - all captured by an objective function and solved iteratively. We implement these ideas in STLts-Div, a lightweight Python tool that integrates with Gurobi.

AI.tldr: STLts-Div generates diverse system traces satisfying STL specifications using MILP with three diversification objectives.
AI.motivation: Engineers need diverse concrete executions to understand STL specifications, as single witnesses are insufficient for exploring edge cases and intent.
AI.method: Builds on MILP encoding of STL and system model, formalizes three diversification objectives (Boolean distance, random Boolean distance, value distance) captured by objective function and solved iteratively.
AI.result: STLts-Div implementation in lightweight Python tool that integrates with Gurobi solver.
AI.conclusion: Diversified trace synthesis provides informative sets of behaviorally diverse traces to aid STL specification understanding and exploration.

title: Distributed Equilibrium-Seeking in Target Coverage Games via Self-Configurable Networks under Limited Communication
summary: We study a target coverage problem in which a team of sensing agents, operating under limited communication, must collaboratively monitor targets that may be adaptively repositioned by an attacker. We model this interaction as a zero-sum game between the sensing team (known as the defender) and the attacker. However, computing an exact Nash equilibrium (NE) for this game is computationally prohibitive as the action space of the defender grows exponentially with the number of sensors and their possible orientations. Exploiting the submodularity property of the game's utility function, we propose a distributed framework that enables agents to self-configure their communication neighborhoods under bandwidth constraints and collaboratively maximize the target coverage. We establish theoretical guarantees showing that the resulting sensing strategies converge to an approximate NE of the game. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed, communication-aware approach that scales effectively for games with combinatorial action spaces while explicitly incorporating communication constraints. To this end, we leverage the distributed bandit-submodular optimization framework and the notion of Value of Coordination that were introduced in [1]. Through simulations, we show that our approach attains near-optimal game value and higher target coverage compared to baselines.

AI.tldr: A distributed framework for sensor teams to collaboratively monitor targets against adaptive attackers, using submodular optimization to achieve approximate Nash equilibrium under communication constraints.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of target coverage by sensor teams operating under limited communication, where an attacker can adaptively reposition targets. Computing exact Nash equilibria is computationally prohibitive due to exponential growth of defender's action space with sensors and orientations.
AI.method: Proposes a distributed framework exploiting submodularity of the utility function. Agents self-configure communication neighborhoods under bandwidth constraints to collaboratively maximize target coverage. Leverages distributed bandit-submodular optimization framework and Value of Coordination concept from prior work.
AI.result: Theoretical guarantees show sensing strategies converge to approximate Nash equilibrium. Simulations demonstrate the approach attains near-optimal game value and higher target coverage compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: This is the first distributed, communication-aware approach that scales effectively for games with combinatorial action spaces while explicitly incorporating communication constraints, enabling sensor teams to achieve robust target coverage against adaptive attackers.

title: Real-Time, Crowdsourcing-Enhanced Forecasting of Building Functionality During Urban Floods
summary: Urban flood emergency response increasingly relies on infrastructure impact forecasts rather than hazard variables alone. However, real-time predictions are unreliable due to biased rainfall, incomplete flood knowledge, and sparse observations. Conventional open-loop forecasting propagates impacts without adjusting the system state, causing errors during critical decisions. This study presents CRAF (Crowdsourcing-Enhanced Real-Time Awareness and Forecasting), a physics-informed, closed-loop framework that converts sparse human-sensed evidence into rolling, decision-grade impact forecasts. By coupling physics-based simulation learning with crowdsourced observations, CRAF infers system conditions from incomplete data and propagates them forward to produce multi-step, real-time predictions of zone-level building functionality loss without online retraining. This closed-loop design supports continuous state correction and forward prediction under weakly structured data with low-latency operation. Offline evaluation demonstrates stable generalization across diverse storm scenarios. In operational deployment during Typhoon Haikui (2023) in Fuzhou, China, CRAF reduces 1-3 hour-ahead forecast errors by 84-95% relative to fixed rainfall-driven forecasting and by 73-80% relative to updated rainfall-driven forecasting, while limiting computation to 10 minutes per update cycle. These results show that impact-state alignment-rather than hazard refinement alone-is essential for reliable real-time decision support, providing a pathway toward operational digital twins for resilient urban infrastructure systems.

AI.tldr: CRAF is a physics-informed closed-loop framework that uses crowdsourced human observations to improve real-time urban flood impact forecasting, reducing forecast errors by 73-95% compared to conventional methods.
AI.motivation: Urban flood emergency response needs reliable impact forecasts, but current real-time predictions are unreliable due to biased rainfall data, incomplete flood knowledge, and sparse observations. Conventional open-loop forecasting propagates errors without state adjustment during critical decision-making.
AI.method: CRAF (Crowdsourcing-Enhanced Real-Time Awareness and Forecasting) is a physics-informed closed-loop framework that couples physics-based simulation learning with crowdsourced observations. It converts sparse human-sensed evidence into rolling impact forecasts, infers system conditions from incomplete data, and propagates them forward to produce multi-step, real-time predictions of zone-level building functionality loss without online retraining.
AI.result: Offline evaluation shows stable generalization across diverse storm scenarios. In operational deployment during Typhoon Haikui (2023) in Fuzhou, China, CRAF reduces 1-3 hour-ahead forecast errors by 84-95% relative to fixed rainfall-driven forecasting and by 73-80% relative to updated rainfall-driven forecasting, while limiting computation to 10 minutes per update cycle.
AI.conclusion: Impact-state alignment—rather than hazard refinement alone—is essential for reliable real-time decision support. CRAF provides a pathway toward operational digital twins for resilient urban infrastructure systems by enabling continuous state correction and forward prediction under weakly structured data with low-latency operation.

title: PowerDAG: Reliable Agentic AI System for Automating Distribution Grid Analysis
summary: This paper introduces PowerDAG, an agentic AI system for automating complex distribution-grid analysis. We address the reliability challenges of state-of-the-art agentic systems in automating complex engineering workflows by introducing two innovative active mechanisms: (i) \textbf{adaptive retrieval}, which uses a similarity-decay cutoff algorithm to dynamically select the most relevant annotated exemplars as context, and (ii) \textbf{just-in-time (JIT) supervision}, which actively intercepts and corrects tool-usage violations during execution. On a benchmark of unseen distribution grid analysis queries, PowerDAG achieves a 100\% success rate with GPT-5.2 and 94.4--96.7\% with smaller open-source models, outperforming base ReAct (41--88\%), LangChain (30--90\%), and CrewAI (9--41\%) baselines by margins of 6--50 percentage points.

AI.tldr: PowerDAG is an agentic AI system that automates complex distribution-grid analysis using adaptive retrieval and just-in-time supervision to improve reliability, achieving near-perfect success rates on benchmark queries.
AI.motivation: Address reliability challenges in state-of-the-art agentic systems for automating complex engineering workflows, particularly in distribution-grid analysis where current systems have inconsistent performance.
AI.method: Introduces two active mechanisms: (1) adaptive retrieval using similarity-decay cutoff algorithm to dynamically select relevant annotated exemplars as context, and (2) just-in-time supervision that actively intercepts and corrects tool-usage violations during execution.
AI.result: Achieves 100% success rate with GPT-5.2 and 94.4-96.7% with smaller open-source models on unseen distribution grid analysis queries, outperforming ReAct (41-88%), LangChain (30-90%), and CrewAI (9-41%) baselines by 6-50 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: PowerDAG demonstrates that active mechanisms like adaptive retrieval and just-in-time supervision can significantly improve the reliability of agentic AI systems for complex engineering workflows, enabling robust automation of distribution-grid analysis tasks.

title: A Tutorial on Learning-Based Radio Map Construction: Data, Paradigms, and Physics-Awarenes
summary: The integration of artificial intelligence into next-generation wireless networks necessitates the accurate construction of radio maps (RMs) as a foundational prerequisite for electromagnetic digital twins. A RM provides the digital representation of the wireless propagation environment, mapping complex geographical and topological boundary conditions to critical spatial-spectral metrics that range from received signal strength to full channel state information matrices. This tutorial presents a comprehensive survey of learning-based RM construction, systematically addressing three intertwined dimensions: data, paradigms, and physics-awareness. From the data perspective, we review physical measurement campaigns, ray tracing simulation engines, and publicly available benchmark datasets, identifying their respective strengths and fundamental limitations. From the paradigm perspective, we establish a core taxonomy that categorizes RM construction into source-aware forward prediction and source-agnostic inverse reconstruction, and examine five principal neural architecture families spanning convolutional neural networks, vision transformers, graph neural networks, generative adversarial networks, and diffusion models. We further survey optics-inspired methods adapted from neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian splatting for continuous wireless radiation field modeling. From the physics-awareness perspective, we introduce a three-level integration framework encompassing data-level feature engineering, loss-level partial differential equation regularization, and architecture-level structural isomorphism. Open challenges including foundation model development, physical hallucination detection, and amortized inference for real-time deployment are discussed to outline future research directions.

AI.tldr: Comprehensive survey of learning-based radio map construction for wireless networks, covering data sources, neural architectures, and physics-aware integration methods.
AI.motivation: The integration of AI into next-generation wireless networks requires accurate radio maps as a foundational prerequisite for electromagnetic digital twins, providing digital representations of wireless propagation environments.
AI.method: Systematic survey addressing three dimensions: data (measurement campaigns, ray tracing, benchmark datasets), paradigms (taxonomy of forward prediction vs. inverse reconstruction with five neural architecture families), and physics-awareness (three-level integration framework).
AI.result: Establishes comprehensive taxonomy and framework for radio map construction, identifies strengths/limitations of data sources, categorizes neural architectures, and proposes physics-aware integration methods.
AI.conclusion: Identifies open challenges including foundation model development, physical hallucination detection, and amortized inference for real-time deployment, outlining future research directions for learning-based radio map construction.

title: Distributed Adaptive Control for DC Power Distribution in Hybrid-Electric Aircraft: Design and Experimental Validation
summary: To reduce CO2 emissions and tackle increasing fuel costs, the aviation industry is swiftly moving towards the electrification of aircraft. From the viewpoint of systems and control, a key challenge brought by this transition corresponds to the management and safe operation of the propulsion system's onboard electrical power distribution network. In this work, for a series-hybrid-electric propulsion system, we propose a distributed adaptive controller for regulating the voltage of a DC bus that energizes the electricity-based propulsion system. The proposed controller -- whose design is based on principles of back-stepping, adaptive, and passivity-based control techniques -- also enables the proportional sharing of the electric load among multiple converter-interfaced sources, which reduces the likelihood of over-stressing individual sources. Compared to existing control strategies, our method ensures stable, convergent, and accurate voltage regulation and load-sharing even if the effects of power lines of unknown resistances and inductances are considered. The performance of the proposed control scheme is experimentally validated and compared to state-of-the-art controllers in a power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) environment.

AI.tldr: A distributed adaptive controller for DC bus voltage regulation and load-sharing in series-hybrid-electric aircraft propulsion systems, addressing unknown line impedances.
AI.motivation: The aviation industry's shift toward electrification to reduce CO2 emissions and fuel costs creates challenges in managing onboard electrical power distribution networks, particularly for safe operation of propulsion systems.
AI.method: A distributed adaptive controller based on back-stepping, adaptive, and passivity-based control techniques for regulating DC bus voltage and enabling proportional load-sharing among multiple converter-interfaced sources.
AI.result: The controller ensures stable, convergent, and accurate voltage regulation and load-sharing even with unknown power line resistances and inductances, validated experimentally in a power hardware-in-the-loop environment.
AI.conclusion: The proposed distributed adaptive controller effectively addresses key challenges in hybrid-electric aircraft propulsion systems, providing robust voltage regulation and load-sharing capabilities superior to existing control strategies.

title: Optimal Control for Steady Circulation of a Diffusion Process via Spectral Decomposition of Fokker-Planck Equation
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS) and CDC 2026
summary: We present a formulation of an optimal control problem for a two-dimensional diffusion process governed by a Fokker-Planck equation to achieve a nonequilibrium steady state with a desired circulation while accelerating convergence toward the stationary distribution. To achieve the control objective, we introduce costs for both the probability density function and flux rotation to the objective functional. We formulate the optimal control problem through dimensionality reduction of the Fokker-Planck equation via eigenfunction expansion, which requires a low-computational cost. We demonstrate that the proposed optimal control achieves the desired circulation while accelerating convergence to the stationary distribution through numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: Optimal control formulation for 2D diffusion processes using Fokker-Planck equation to achieve desired circulation in nonequilibrium steady states while accelerating convergence to stationary distribution.
AI.motivation: To develop control methods for achieving specific circulation patterns in nonequilibrium steady states of diffusion processes while improving convergence rates to stationary distributions.
AI.method: Formulate optimal control problem with costs for probability density function and flux rotation, using dimensionality reduction via eigenfunction expansion of Fokker-Planck equation for computational efficiency.
AI.result: Numerical simulations demonstrate successful achievement of desired circulation patterns while accelerating convergence to stationary distribution.
AI.conclusion: The proposed optimal control framework effectively controls 2D diffusion processes to achieve target circulation in nonequilibrium steady states with improved convergence properties.

title: An Extended T-A Formulation Based on Potential-Chain Recursion for Electromagnetic Modeling of Parallel-Wound No-Insulation HTS Coils
summary: Parallel-wound no-insulation (PW-NI) high-temperature superconducting (HTS) coils significantly reduce charging delay while maintaining excellent self-protection capability, demonstrating great potential for high-field applications. Existing models that couple the T-A formulation with equivalent circuits have demonstrated high accuracy in electromagnetic analysis of PW-NI coils. However, eliminating the computational overhead caused by frequent variable mapping and data exchange between electromagnetic and circuit modules is important for improving computational efficiency, particularly in long-duration transient simulations of large-scale magnets. To address this issue, an extended T-A formulation based on potential-chain recursion, termed PCR-TA, is proposed. By directly embedding inter-tape current sharing and radial current bypass behaviors into the finite-element framework, this method computes the transient electromagnetic response of PW-NI coils without requiring an explicit equivalent circuit model. Building upon it, a multi-scale approach is further developed for large-scale PW-NI coils. The validity of the proposed method and its multi-scale extension is verified through comparisons with experimental measurements and field-circuit coupled modeling results. Comparative analyses demonstrate that the PCR-TA method achieves a speedup of approximately 2.4 over the field-circuit coupled method, whereas its multi-scale extension further increases this speedup to roughly 5.8.
