Furthermore, the PCR-TA method is extended to model the continuous transition of PW-NI coils from power-supply charging to closed-loop operation. This work provides an efficient method and tool for the electromagnetic modeling of PW-NI coils under both driven and closed-loop operating conditions.

AI.tldr: Proposed PCR-TA method extends T-A formulation with potential-chain recursion for efficient electromagnetic modeling of parallel-wound no-insulation HTS coils, eliminating circuit coupling overhead and achieving 2.4-5.8× speedup.
AI.motivation: Existing field-circuit coupled models for PW-NI HTS coils suffer from computational inefficiency due to frequent variable mapping and data exchange between electromagnetic and circuit modules, especially problematic for long-duration transient simulations of large-scale magnets.
AI.method: Developed PCR-TA (potential-chain recursion T-A) formulation that directly embeds inter-tape current sharing and radial current bypass behaviors into finite-element framework, eliminating explicit equivalent circuit model. Extended to multi-scale approach for large-scale PW-NI coils and continuous transition modeling from power-supply charging to closed-loop operation.
AI.result: PCR-TA method achieves ~2.4× speedup over field-circuit coupled method; multi-scale extension further increases speedup to ~5.8×. Method validated against experimental measurements and field-circuit coupled modeling results, demonstrating accurate electromagnetic response computation.
AI.conclusion: PCR-TA provides efficient electromagnetic modeling tool for PW-NI coils under both driven and closed-loop operating conditions, addressing computational overhead issues while maintaining accuracy for high-field magnet applications.

title: Real-Time Online Learning for Model Predictive Control using a Spatio-Temporal Gaussian Process Approximation
comment: to be published at 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics & Automation (ICRA)
summary: Learning-based model predictive control (MPC) can enhance control performance by correcting for model inaccuracies, enabling more precise state trajectory predictions than traditional MPC. A common approach is to model unknown residual dynamics as a Gaussian process (GP), which leverages data and also provides an estimate of the associated uncertainty. However, the high computational cost of online learning poses a major challenge for real-time GP-MPC applications. This work presents an efficient implementation of an approximate spatio-temporal GP model, offering online learning at constant computational complexity. It is optimized for GP-MPC, where it enables improved control performance by learning more accurate system dynamics online in real-time, even for time-varying systems. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulations and hardware experiments in the exemplary application of autonomous miniature racing.

AI.tldr: Efficient online GP-MPC with constant computational complexity for real-time control of time-varying systems, demonstrated on autonomous racing.
AI.motivation: Traditional MPC suffers from model inaccuracies, while existing GP-MPC approaches have prohibitive computational costs for real-time applications, especially for time-varying systems.
AI.method: Developed an efficient implementation of an approximate spatio-temporal Gaussian process model with constant computational complexity for online learning, optimized specifically for GP-MPC applications.
AI.result: The method enables improved control performance by learning more accurate system dynamics online in real-time, with computational efficiency suitable for real-time applications.
AI.conclusion: The proposed efficient GP-MPC implementation successfully addresses computational bottlenecks, enabling real-time online learning for improved control performance in dynamic systems like autonomous racing.

title: Hierarchical Decision-Making under Uncertainty: A Hybrid MDP and Chance-Constrained MPC Approach
summary: This paper presents a hierarchical decision-making framework for autonomous systems operating under uncertainty, demonstrated through autonomous driving as a representative application. Surrounding agents are modeled using Hybrid Markov Decision Processes (HMDPs) that jointly capture maneuver-level and dynamic-level uncertainties, enabling the multi-modal environmental prediction. The ego agent is modeled using a separate HMDP and integrated into a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that unifies maneuver selection with dynamic feasibility within a single optimization. A set of joint chance constraints serves as the bridge between environmental prediction and optimization, incorporating multi-modal environment predictions into the MPC formulation and ensuring safety across all plausible interaction scenarios. The proposed framework provides theoretical guarantees on recursive feasibility and asymptotic stability, and its benefits in terms of safety and efficiency are validated through comprehensive evaluations in highway and urban environments, together with comparisons against a rule-based baseline.

AI.tldr: Hierarchical decision-making framework for autonomous systems using HMDPs for multi-modal environmental prediction and MPC with joint chance constraints for safety guarantees.
AI.motivation: Autonomous systems need to operate safely under uncertainty with surrounding agents exhibiting multi-modal behaviors, requiring frameworks that can predict diverse interaction scenarios while ensuring safety and efficiency.
AI.method: Hybrid Markov Decision Processes (HMDPs) model surrounding agents for multi-modal prediction; ego agent modeled with separate HMDP integrated into Model Predictive Control (MPC) with joint chance constraints bridging prediction and optimization.
AI.result: Framework provides theoretical guarantees on recursive feasibility and asymptotic stability; validation in highway and urban environments shows improved safety and efficiency compared to rule-based baseline.
AI.conclusion: The hierarchical framework successfully integrates multi-modal environmental prediction with optimization-based control, offering formal safety guarantees and practical benefits for autonomous driving under uncertainty.

title: Defending the power grid by segmenting the EV charging cyber infrastructure
summary: This paper examines defending the power grid against load-altering attacks using electric vehicle charging. It proposes to preventively segment the cyber infrastructure that charging station operators (CSOs) use to communicate with and control their charging stations, thereby limiting the impact of successful cyber-attacks. Using real German charging station data and a reconstructed transmission grid model, a threat analysis shows that without segmentation, the successful hack of just two CSOs can overload two transmission grid branches, exceeding the N-1 security margin and necessitating defense measures. A novel defense design problem is then formulated that minimizes the number of imposed segmentations while bounding the number of branch overloads under worst-case attacks. The resulting IP-MILP bi-level problem can be solved with an exact column and constraint generation algorithm and with heuristics for fast computation on large-scale instances. For the near-real-world Germany case, the applicability of the heuristics is demonstrated and validated under relevant load and dispatch scenarios. It is found that the simple scheme of segmenting CSOs evenly by their installed capacity leads to only 23% more segments compared to the heuristic optimization result, suggesting potential relevance as a regulatory measure.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes cyber infrastructure segmentation for electric vehicle charging stations to defend power grids against load-altering attacks, showing that hacking just two charging station operators can overload transmission lines and presenting optimization methods to minimize segmentations while bounding grid overloads.
AI.motivation: The power grid faces threats from load-altering attacks through electric vehicle charging infrastructure. Without proper defenses, successful cyber-attacks on charging station operators could overload transmission grid branches, exceeding security margins and potentially causing grid instability.
AI.method: The paper proposes preventive segmentation of cyber infrastructure used by charging station operators to control charging stations. It formulates a defense design problem as an IP-MILP bi-level optimization that minimizes segmentations while bounding branch overloads under worst-case attacks. Both exact column and constraint generation algorithms and heuristics are developed for large-scale instances.
AI.result: Using real German charging station data and transmission grid models, threat analysis shows that hacking just two charging station operators can overload two transmission branches, exceeding N-1 security. For the Germany case, heuristics demonstrate applicability under various load scenarios, and a simple capacity-based segmentation scheme requires only 23% more segments than optimized solutions.
AI.conclusion: Cyber infrastructure segmentation of electric vehicle charging stations provides effective defense against load-altering attacks on power grids. The proposed optimization methods enable efficient segmentation planning, and simple capacity-based segmentation schemes show promise as practical regulatory measures for grid security.

title: On maximal positive invariant set computation for rank-deficient linear systems
summary:
The maximal positively invariant (MPI) set is obtained through a backward reachability procedure involving the iterative computation and intersection of predecessor sets under state and input constraints.
  However, standard static feedback synthesis may place some of the closed-loop eigenvalues at zero, leading to rank-deficient dynamics. This affects the MPI computation by inducing projections onto lower-dimensional subspaces during intermediate steps. By exploiting the Schur decomposition, we explicitly address this singular case and propose a robust algorithm that computes the MPI set in both polyhedral and constrained-zonotope representations.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses MPI set computation for systems with rank-deficient dynamics (eigenvalues at zero), proposing a robust algorithm using Schur decomposition for both polyhedral and constrained-zonotope representations.
AI.motivation: Standard static feedback synthesis can place closed-loop eigenvalues at zero, creating rank-deficient dynamics that affect MPI set computation by inducing projections onto lower-dimensional subspaces during backward reachability procedures.
AI.method: Exploits Schur decomposition to explicitly address the singular case, proposes a robust algorithm that computes the maximal positively invariant (MPI) set through backward reachability with predecessor sets under constraints, handling both polyhedral and constrained-zonotope representations.
AI.result: Develops a computational framework that properly handles rank-deficient dynamics in MPI set computation, enabling accurate determination of invariant sets for systems with singular dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Schur decomposition-based approach provides a robust solution for MPI set computation in systems with rank-deficient dynamics, overcoming limitations of standard methods that fail to properly handle projections onto lower-dimensional subspaces.

title: Robust Dynamic Pricing and Admission Control with Fairness Guarantees
summary: Dynamic pricing is commonly used to regulate congestion in shared service systems. This paper is motivated by the fact that when heterogeneaous user groups (in terms of price responsiveness) are present, conventional monotonic pricing can lead to unfair outcomes by disproportionately excluding price-elastic users, particularly under high or uncertain demand. The paper's contributions are twofold. First, we show that when fairness is imposed as a hard state constraint, the optimal (revenue maximizing) pricing policy is generally non-monotonic in demand. This structural result departs fundamentally from standard surge pricing rules and reveals that price reduction under heavy load may be necessary to maintain equitable access. Second, we address the problem that price elasticity among heterogeneous users is unobservable. To solve it, we develop a robust dynamic pricing and admission control framework that enforces resource capacity and fairness constraints for all user type distributions consistent with aggregate measurements. By integrating integral High Order Control Barrier Functions (iHOCBFs) with a worst case robust optimization framework, we obtain a controller that guarantees forward invariance of safety and fairness constraints while optimizing revenue. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved fairness and revenue performance relative to monotonic surge pricing policies.

AI.tldr: Optimal dynamic pricing for heterogeneous users requires non-monotonic pricing to ensure fairness, with robust control framework handling unobservable price elasticity.
AI.motivation: Conventional monotonic surge pricing in shared service systems can create unfair outcomes by disproportionately excluding price-elastic users, especially under high or uncertain demand when heterogeneous user groups with different price responsiveness are present.
AI.method: Develops a robust dynamic pricing and admission control framework that enforces resource capacity and fairness constraints for all user type distributions consistent with aggregate measurements. Integrates integral High Order Control Barrier Functions (iHOCBFs) with worst-case robust optimization to guarantee forward invariance of safety and fairness constraints while optimizing revenue.
AI.result: Shows that when fairness is imposed as a hard state constraint, optimal revenue-maximizing pricing policy is generally non-monotonic in demand, requiring price reduction under heavy load to maintain equitable access. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved fairness and revenue performance compared to monotonic surge pricing policies.
AI.conclusion: Fairness constraints fundamentally change optimal pricing structure, requiring non-monotonic policies. The proposed robust control framework successfully handles unobservable price elasticity while guaranteeing constraint satisfaction and improving both fairness and revenue outcomes.

title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Stochastic Descriptor Systems: An Innovation-Based Approach Handling Non-Causal Dynamics
summary: Descriptor systems arise naturally in applications governed by algebraic constraints, such as power networks and chemical processes. The singular system matrix in descriptor systems may introduce non-causal dynamics, where the current output depends on future inputs and, in the presence of stochastic process and measurement noise, on future noise realizations as well. This paper proposes a data-driven predictive control framework for stochastic descriptor systems that accommodates algebraic constraints and impulsive modes without explicit system identification. A causal innovation representation is constructed by augmenting the system state with a noise buffer that encapsulates the non-causal stochastic interactions, transforming the descriptor system into an equivalent proper state-space form. Willems' Fundamental Lemma is then extended to the innovation form with fully data-verifiable conditions. Building on these results, a practical Inno-DeePC algorithm is developed that integrates offline innovation estimation and online predictive control. Numerical experiments on a direct-current (DC) microgrid demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for stochastic descriptor systems.

AI.tldr: Data-driven predictive control for stochastic descriptor systems using innovation representation and Willems' Fundamental Lemma extension, demonstrated on DC microgrid.
AI.motivation: Descriptor systems with algebraic constraints (e.g., power networks, chemical processes) have singular system matrices that introduce non-causal dynamics where current outputs depend on future inputs and noise. Existing methods require explicit system identification, which is challenging for stochastic descriptor systems with impulsive modes.
AI.method: Proposes a causal innovation representation by augmenting system state with a noise buffer to encapsulate non-causal stochastic interactions, transforming descriptor system into equivalent proper state-space form. Extends Willems' Fundamental Lemma to innovation form with fully data-verifiable conditions. Develops Inno-DeePC algorithm integrating offline innovation estimation and online predictive control.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on a direct-current (DC) microgrid demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach for stochastic descriptor systems, showing successful handling of algebraic constraints and impulsive modes without explicit system identification.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a practical data-driven predictive control solution for stochastic descriptor systems that accommodates algebraic constraints and impulsive modes, eliminating the need for explicit system identification while maintaining causal relationships through innovation representation.

title: An HMDP-MPC Decision-making Framework with Adaptive Safety Margins and Hysteresis for Autonomous Driving
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, to be published in ICRA 2026 proceedings
summary: This paper presents a unified decision-making framework that integrates Hybrid Markov Decision Processes (HMDPs) with Model Predictive Control (MPC), augmented by velocity-dependent safety margins and a prediction-aware hysteresis mechanism. Both the ego and surrounding vehicles are modeled as HMDPs, allowing discrete maneuver transition and kinematic evolution to be jointly considered within the MPC optimization. Safety margins derived from the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) adapt to traffic context but vary with speed, which can cause oscillatory decisions and velocity fluctuations. To mitigate this, we propose a frozen-release hysteresis mechanism with distinct trigger and release thresholds, effectively enlarging the reaction buffer and suppressing oscillations. Decision continuity is further safeguarded by a two-layer recovery scheme: a global bounded relaxation tied to IDM margins and a deterministic fallback policy. The framework is evaluated through a case study, an ablation against a no-hysteresis baseline, and largescale randomized experiments across 18 traffic settings. Across 8,050 trials, it achieves a collision rate of only 0.05%, with 98.77% of decisions resolved by nominal MPC and minimal reliance on relaxation or fallback. These results demonstrate the robustness and adaptability of the proposed decision-making framework in heterogeneous traffic conditions.

AI.tldr: A unified decision-making framework combining Hybrid Markov Decision Processes with Model Predictive Control, featuring adaptive safety margins and hysteresis mechanisms for robust autonomous driving in heterogeneous traffic.
AI.motivation: To address oscillatory decisions and velocity fluctuations caused by speed-dependent safety margins in autonomous driving systems, and to create a robust decision-making framework that maintains decision continuity while ensuring safety in heterogeneous traffic conditions.
AI.method: Integrates Hybrid Markov Decision Processes (HMDPs) with Model Predictive Control (MPC), using velocity-dependent safety margins from Intelligent Driver Model (IDM), a frozen-release hysteresis mechanism with distinct trigger/release thresholds, and a two-layer recovery scheme with global bounded relaxation and deterministic fallback policy.
AI.result: Achieved 0.05% collision rate across 8,050 trials in 18 traffic settings, with 98.77% of decisions resolved by nominal MPC and minimal reliance on relaxation/fallback mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework demonstrates robust performance and adaptability in heterogeneous traffic conditions, effectively suppressing oscillations while maintaining safety through integrated HMDP-MPC optimization and sophisticated hysteresis mechanisms.

title: Verification and Validation of Physics-Informed Surrogate Component Models for Dynamic Power-System Simulation
summary: Physics-informed machine learning surrogates are increasingly explored to accelerate dynamic simulation of generators, converters, and other power grid components. The key question, however, is not only whether a surrogate matches a stand-alone component model on average, but whether it remains accurate after insertion into a differential-algebraic simulator, where the surrogate outputs enter the algebraic equations coupling the component to the rest of the system. This paper formulates that in-simulator use as a verification and validation (V\&V) problem. A finite-horizon bound is derived that links allowable component-output error to algebraic-coupling sensitivity, dynamic error amplification, and the simulation horizon. Two complementary settings are then studied: model-based verification against a reference component solver, and data-based validation through conformal calibration of the component-output variables exchanged with the simulator. The framework is general, but the case study focuses on physics-informed neural-network surrogates of second-, fourth-, and sixth-order synchronous-machine models. Results show that good stand-alone surrogate accuracy does not by itself guarantee accurate in-simulator behavior, that the largest discrepancies concentrate in stressed operating regions, and that small equation residuals do not necessarily imply small state-trajectory errors.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a verification and validation framework for physics-informed machine learning surrogates in power grid simulations, showing that good stand-alone accuracy doesn't guarantee accurate in-simulator behavior.
AI.motivation: Physics-informed ML surrogates are used to accelerate power grid component simulations, but there's a need to verify their accuracy when integrated into differential-algebraic simulators where surrogate outputs affect algebraic coupling equations.
AI.method: Formulates in-simulator use as a V&V problem, derives finite-horizon bounds linking component-output error to algebraic-coupling sensitivity and dynamic error amplification, and studies model-based verification against reference solvers and data-based validation through conformal calibration.
AI.result: Good stand-alone surrogate accuracy doesn't guarantee accurate in-simulator behavior, largest discrepancies occur in stressed operating regions, and small equation residuals don't necessarily imply small state-trajectory errors.
AI.conclusion: A systematic V&V framework is essential for ensuring physics-informed ML surrogates maintain accuracy when integrated into power grid simulators, with particular attention needed for stressed operating conditions.

title: Koopman Generator Decomposition for Port-Hamiltonian System
comment: 8 pages; submitted to IEEE Conference on Decision and Control, 2026
summary: We establish a canonical decomposition of the infinitesimal Koopman generator of any port-Hamiltonian (pH) system into skew-adjoint (energy-conserving), positive-semidefinite (dissipative), and input-port components, proving that the generator satisfies an energy-dissipation inequality on a dense subdomain of $L^2(μ)$ for any invariant measure $μ$ satisfying a mild joint-invariance condition stated in Theorem 1. This infinite-dimensional splitting carries over exactly to finite-dimensional Galerkin approximations, yielding structure-constrained surrogate models that provably inherit passivity with a quadratic storage function in the lifted observable space. Leveraging this structure, we design passivity-based controllers directly in the lifted space and establish asymptotic stability of the lifted closed-loop system via LaSalle's invariance principle under a mild detectability condition. For linear pH systems, the decomposition recovers the true pH matrices exactly, confirming that the structural constraints arise naturally from the operator theory rather than being imposed by hand. The framework unifies port-Hamiltonian systems theory and Koopman spectral methods, providing a rigorous operator-theoretic foundation for energy-consistent lifting of nonlinear pH dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a canonical decomposition of the Koopman generator for port-Hamiltonian systems into energy-conserving, dissipative, and input-port components, providing a rigorous operator-theoretic foundation for energy-consistent lifting of nonlinear pH dynamics.
AI.motivation: To bridge port-Hamiltonian systems theory and Koopman spectral methods by providing a rigorous operator-theoretic foundation for energy-consistent lifting of nonlinear pH dynamics, enabling structure-preserving approximations and passivity-based control design.
AI.method: Establishes a canonical decomposition of the infinitesimal Koopman generator for any port-Hamiltonian system into skew-adjoint (energy-conserving), positive-semidefinite (dissipative), and input-port components. Proves the generator satisfies an energy-dissipation inequality on a dense subdomain of L²(μ) for invariant measures. Shows this decomposition carries over exactly to finite-dimensional Galerkin approximations, yielding structure-constrained surrogate models.
AI.result: The decomposition recovers the true pH matrices exactly for linear pH systems, confirming structural constraints arise naturally from operator theory. The framework enables design of passivity-based controllers directly in the lifted space and establishes asymptotic stability of the lifted closed-loop system via LaSalle's invariance principle under mild detectability conditions.
AI.conclusion: The paper unifies port-Hamiltonian systems theory and Koopman spectral methods, providing a rigorous operator-theoretic foundation for energy-consistent lifting of nonlinear pH dynamics. The decomposition yields structure-preserving approximations that inherit passivity properties, enabling principled control design in the lifted observable space.

title: Real-time Coordination of Cascaded Hydroelectric Generation under Decision-Dependent Uncertainties
summary: This paper proposes a real-time control policy for cascaded hydropower systems that incorporates decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) to capture the coupling of streamflow uncertainties across the network. The framework jointly models exogenous forecast errors and endogenous uncertainty propagation, explicitly characterizing the dependence between upstream releases and downstream inflow variability through a heteroskedastic variance model conditioned on past errors, variance, and control actions. We formulate a joint chance-constrained optimization problem to ensure reliable system operation under uncertainty, and develop a tractable supporting hyperplane algorithm that enables explicit and adaptive risk allocation under DDU. We establish convergence of the proposed method and show that it recovers the Bonferroni approximation under steady-state conditions. A randomized case study based on Columbia River data demonstrates that the proposed framework improves both energy generation and reservoir reliability by accounting for DDU. Sensitivity analyses on drought severity and model parameters further highlight the value of adaptive risk allocation for resilient hydropower operations.

AI.tldr: Real-time control policy for cascaded hydropower systems incorporating decision-dependent uncertainty (DDU) to capture streamflow uncertainty coupling, with joint chance-constrained optimization and tractable supporting hyperplane algorithm for adaptive risk allocation.
AI.motivation: Traditional hydropower control policies often treat streamflow uncertainties as independent or exogenous, failing to capture the coupling of uncertainties across cascaded systems where upstream releases affect downstream inflow variability, necessitating a framework that models both exogenous forecast errors and endogenous uncertainty propagation.
AI.method: Proposes a framework that jointly models exogenous forecast errors and endogenous uncertainty propagation through a heteroskedastic variance model conditioned on past errors, variance, and control actions. Formulates a joint chance-constrained optimization problem and develops a tractable supporting hyperplane algorithm for explicit and adaptive risk allocation under decision-dependent uncertainty.
AI.result: The method establishes convergence and recovers the Bonferroni approximation under steady-state conditions. A randomized case study based on Columbia River data demonstrates improved energy generation and reservoir reliability by accounting for DDU. Sensitivity analyses highlight the value of adaptive risk allocation for resilient hydropower operations under varying drought severity and model parameters.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively captures decision-dependent uncertainty in cascaded hydropower systems, providing both theoretical guarantees and practical benefits through improved operational performance and adaptive risk management, offering a valuable tool for resilient hydropower operations under uncertainty.
